title: Systems Engineer, Corporate Security
description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year - far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Corporate Security at Ramp owns the security of our internal environment: the device fleet, the identity and access layer, and the AI tools employees use for their work. We are hiring a Systems Engineer to build and operate the controls across these systems.

The role is hands-on, writing code and building agentic loops wherever possible rather than solving problems manually. You will help manage device configuration and patching via configuration-as-code, authentication and authenticator policies in Okta, network and gateway enforcement in Cloudflare, and the controls around our enterprise Claude and OpenAI deployments. These systems overlap heavily in practice, and the work is largely about integrating them and automating what would otherwise be manual administration.

You will report to the Corporate Security lead and work closely with IT, Security Engineering, and AI DevX.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Maintain update policies for both OS and software, and monitor the fleet so that newly introduced applications are brought into the patching cadence

- Build automation for endpoint security agent remediation across EDR, DLP, VPN, and similar tooling - detecting missing, stale, or unhealthy agents and bringing devices back into compliance

- Maintain device configuration baselines as code, including drift detection and hardening standards

- Configure authentication and authenticator policies in Okta: SSO, MFA and authenticator enrollment, device trust, and conditional access

- Remediate identity posture gaps surfaced by ISPM tooling: stale accounts, orphaned service principals, over-scoped OAuth grants, MFA gaps, and excess privileges

- Implement and operate controls for enterprise AI usage, including identity-aware access, logging and retention, DLP where appropriate, and enforcement

- Automate across these platforms using their APIs, build reporting on control coverage, and document how the controls you build are operated

WHAT YOU NEED

- 3-5 years of experience in Client Platform Engineer/Endpoint Engineering, Identity Access & Management, or Corporate Security

- Hands-on macOS management at scale: MDM (Jamf, Fleet, Kandji, or equivalent) and macOS update mechanisms

- Working knowledge of an identity provider (Okta or similar): SSO, authentication and authenticator policies, SCIM provisioning, and conditional access

- Scripting ability in Python, Go, or Bash, and experience automating against platform APIs

- Experience with EDR and endpoint vulnerability management (CrowdStrike or similar)

- Ability to evaluate tradeoffs between technical enforcement, policy, and user friction, and to explain those tradeoffs clearly

NICE TO HAVE

- osquery and Fleet, or other query-based fleet visibility tooling

- Identity posture management (ISPM) tooling, or access review and governance platforms

- Cloudflare Zero Trust, or other proxy, DNS, or network-layer enforcement, including TLS inspection

- Exposure to AI and LLM security concerns: agent authorization, tool calls, model gateways, data lea

ABOUT US

At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.

With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.

Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Deployed Engineer to join our Professional Services team, working directly with enterprise customers to build reliable, production agents. You'll translate vague enterprise workflows into concrete software specs and guide engineering teams through the resulting solution, or build it for them. You might spend a week designing a customer's agent architecture, a few weeks co-building their evaluation pipeline, or a quarter embedded inside their team shipping alongside their engineers. You are someone who's built real AI systems for production and can defend the technical tradeoffs within them.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Advising: Agent architecture design, evaluation strategy review, and best-practice production guidance.

- Building: Co-build with the customer's engineering team across the full Agent Development Lifecycle (ADLC) in outcome-scoped engagements.

- Embedding: Serve as a deployed engineer inside the customer's team for extended engagements, operating as a de facto member of their org to ship agent systems directly.

- Agent Engineering: ADLC end-to-end, architecture design, orchestration patterns, evals, custom conversational UIs, and production deployment.

- Applied AI: Post-training, supervised fine-tuning, harness engineering, trace mining, model selection and evaluation methodology.

REQUIREMENTS

- 4+ years of software engineering experience with deep expertise in Python. TypeScript/JavaScript a plus.

- 2+ years of hands-on experience building and shipping production agent systems.

- Strong client-facing communication skills, with the ability to confidently articulate architectural decisions to technical stakeholders (engineers, architects, CTOs).

- Strong experience with LangChain/LangGraph/Deep Agents or comparable frameworks, including multi-agent patterns and state management (short and long-term memory).

- Deep familiarity designing and implementing evaluation methodologies for non-deterministic AI systems.

- Comfortable operating across the full spectrum from advisory to embedded delivery.

- Willing to travel up to 20% of the time.

NICE TO HAVE

- Exposure to dataset curation and post-training techniques (SFT, DPO, RLHF) on open-weight models using tools like Axolotl, Unsloth, Hugging Face transformers, or TRL.

- Experience with trace mining to drive continuous improvement loops

Remote in Singapore

title: Email Coordinator
description:
About This Role

This is a guest-facing email coordination role at a fast-growing luxury travel and concierge company. Day-
to-day, you’ll be the primary link between guests and the hotels and suppliers that make their experiences

exceptional - gathering trip details, communicating guest preferences to hotels, and ensuring every
interaction is warm, accurate, and on-brand. Rate checking is part of the role, but communication is the
core of it. This is not a task-and-log-off role. Full presence, proactive thinking, and genuine ownership are

expected throughout every shift.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Guest & Hotel Email Coordination (Primary)

• Work with guests via email to gather trip information - preferences, special requests, ETAs, and any last-minute

needs.

• Communicate these details to hotels and suppliers ahead of each arrival, ensuring nothing is missed regardless
of whether the client has replied.
• Handle VIP1 & VIP2 pre-arrival touchpoints: confirm arrivals, brief hotels, and follow up with both parties as
needed.
• Maintain a warm, personal, on-brand tone in every message - it should never read like a template.

Rate Checking (Supporting)

• When a booking comes in, verify the guest has the best available rate by checking the hotel’s public website
and/or booking engine - this is confirmation and verification, not proactive deal-hunting.
• Where needed, contact the hotel directly for pricing and information.
• Flag rate discrepancies and document findings accurately - this is investigative, detail-driven work.
• Occasional quoting may be required; when it is, the focus is on retrieving accurate pricing through the right
channels, not finding the cheapest option.

High-Volume Email Management

• Log in, scan the full inbox, triage by urgency, and label before actioning - never work top to bottom.
• Prioritise flagged and time-sensitive items first; process supplier confirmations, replies, and new inquiries
systematically.
• Maintain inbox zero by end of shift - nothing unresolved or unacknowledged.

Hotel & Supplier Outreach

• Email hotels and vendors to confirm bookings, flag special requests, and follow up on outstanding items.
• Where email isn’t getting a response, escalate to a call - but keep most communication via email where

possible.

Shift Handovers & Notion

• Update Notion at the end of every shift with open items, actions taken, and anything the next coordinator needs
to pick up.
• Keep SOPs and task notes current so the team always has visibility.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

• Genuine passion for travel - you don’t need a CV full of travel jobs, but you need to actually care about this
space and want to grow in it.
• Thinks on their feet - when something goes sideways, you look for a solution before you escalate.
• Warm, polished written communication - professional but personal, never robotic or templated.
• Attention to detail - you catch what others miss, before it reaches the guest.

• Email triage instinct - you scan, sort, and prioritise; you don’t need to be told what matters most.
• Proactive communicator - if you’re stuck, behind, or unsure, you say so early.
• Comfortable with ambiguity - workflows evolve, and you adapt without needing hand-holding.
• Full commitment - exclusivity required. This role cannot be combined with other employment.

SHIFT & AVAILABILITY

Schedule Hard start and end times - not a task-completion role
Hours 9-hour shift including 1-hour unpaid break (8 productive hours)
Start Time Daytime or evening shift TBD - to be confirmed at offer stage
Weekend At least one weekend day required (e.g. Sun-Thu or Tue-Sat)
Exclusivity No concurrent employment - full focus required from day one

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGY

Email Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets)
Inbox Mgmt Hiver - shared inbox assignments and email tracking

AI Drafting Claude - used to support email drafts and workflow efficiency

Our mission is to elevate the world of manufacturing by introducing intelligent, flexible robots that enhance human capabilities and existing machinery, ushering in the next era of production at higher quality, with less waste, and lower cost.

We see a future where every element of manufacturing, from design to assembly, is optimised with intelligent automation. The role

We are hiring a Chief of Staff to the CEO.

You are the CEO's closest execution partner. You sit in the rooms the CEO sits in, and represent him in the ones he cannot be in. You make sure the company executes fast on the decisions made in those rooms, by driving the most important cross-team projects yourself.

The mandate has four parts. Run the operating cadence the leadership team works inside. Own the company's commitments and see them through to done. Make the CEO's decisions and priorities legible to everyone they affect. Protect the CEO's time for the work only the CEO can do.

This is a senior individual role with no direct reports. Your authority comes from the mandate, agreed in writing with the CEO, and from being right. You are not a gatekeeper.

We are outcome-driven, direct, high trust and high autonomy. There is very little hand-holding. We enjoy working with people who bring a healthy degree of intensity and drive.

- Drive cross-functional execution

- Build and manage the operating system
Morning briefs, commitments tracking, meeting-to-action pipelines, and the reporting the CEO takes to the board. Build the foundation and systems, so the company gets more legible with less manual work. You do this yourself, not through a vendor.

- Make the company legible
Decisions, processes and playbooks written once, findable by everyone, and used as the standard.

- Take special projects, up to a day a week
You pick them up with CEO-level urgency and hand them back completed, or with an owner and a clear path to done.

Who you are

- You bring energy
High intensity, high pace, and you are impatient when good decisions sit. You set the tempo in a room without raising your voice. People move faster because you are there.

- You have operated inside a fast-changing, venture-backed company
Typically four to eight years in. You have lived through at least one moment where the plan changed under you and you kept the team executing. Titles vary: chief of staff, business operations, founder's associate, program or product lead, consultant who went operating, ex-founder. We care

The Role

We are looking for an experienced Automation Engineer to take technical ownership of the Facilities Monitoring and Control System (FMCS) that keeps our fab running - the system that supervises every utility our production depends on, from cleanroom air and chilled water to process cooling, exhaust and power monitoring. The system is delivered and commissioned by an external integrator; from handover, it's yours. - Operate, monitor and maintain our SCADA system (Siemens WinCC OA) across servers, operator stations and displays

- Maintain and diagnose our Siemens S7-1500 PLCs and their remote I/O, and adapt control logic within the existing standardised structure

- Plan and perform loop checks end to end - tracing each signal from the field device through wiring, I/O and PLC all the way to the operator screen, and confirming that commands actually move valves, dampers and actuators

- Investigate and resolve alarms, communication faults and unexpected equipment behaviourduring live operation

- Verify instrument calibration and troubleshoot analog and digital field signals - multimeter in hand, not only from a screen

- Add new datapoints, screens, trends and reports, and tune alarms so operators trust the system

- Keep documentation current - as-built drawings, tag lists, change records - and uphold change control

- Act as the technical counterpart to contractors and vendors, and support qualification and audits with system evidence

- 5+ years of hands-on experience with industrial SCADA and PLC systems in a production environment - commissioning, operating or supporting, not only design

- Solid experience with Siemens S7 PLCs (TIA Portal / Step 7) - going online, reading and modifying logic, diagnosing faults on a running plant; experience with comparable PLC platforms is also welcome

- Strong SCADA engineering skills - ideally Siemens WinCC OA, but experience with another platform (e.g. WinCC, PCS 7, Ignition, Aveva, Zenon) plus the willingness to grow into WinCC OA is just as welcome

- Practical experience with loop checks, instrument calibration and signal troubleshooting, and with reading P&IDs, loop diagrams and I/O lists

- Good command of English; German is a strong advantage given the site, suppliers and local contractors

The Opportunity

Praxis is hiring a highly motivated, detail-obsessed Senior Manager, Congress Operations, to lead our planning for medical and scientific congresses. You will own the congress portfolio end-to-end: setting plans and timelines, managing vendors and budgets, driving cross-functional execution, and ensuring a high-quality onsite experience.

You will partner closely with Medical Affairs, Marketing, Sales, Communications, and Legal / Compliance to bring our science, story, and patient mission to life in a way that is on-brand, compliant, and high impact. Primary Responsibilities

• Own the congress portfolio. Lead planning and execution for medical and scientific congresses-including AAN, AES, EEC and MDS-as well as meetings in the US and abroad. Establish clear objectives, plans, owners, timelines, and measures of success.

• Drive disciplined cross-functional execution. Maintain the integrated congress calendar and critical-path milestones across abstracts, exhibits, housing, registration, freight, and print. Align stakeholders on decisions and dependencies and escalate conflicts early enough to protect delivery.

• Lead and develop the team. Manage the Meeting Planner, setting priorities, ownership, and high standards for execution. Build redundancy and onsite coverage so critical congresses never depend on a single person’s availability or knowledge.

• Deliver seamless onsite execution. Oversee staffing, materials, production, logistics, and real-time troubleshooting. Support speaker engagement logistics, including travel, honoraria, and contracts, in partnership with Medical Affairs and Legal/Compliance.

• Raise the bar with every congress. Capture performance, stakeholder feedback, and lessons learned and turn them into concrete improvements for future events.

• Operate with a strong compliance mindset. Execute congress activities in partnership in accordance with applicable requirements, including the PhRMA Code, Sunshine Act/Open Payments, and fair-market-value requirements.

• 8+ years of experience leading events or congresses in life sciences, biotech, healthcare, or a similarly regulated environment, including direct experience with large-scale medical or scientific congresses.

• Demonstrated people-management experience, or clear readiness to lead and develop a direct report.

• Proven ownership of congress budgets and third-party vendors, including scope, timelines, performance accountability, and escalation.

• Knowledge of relevant industry compliance requirements is a plus.
